storylines.title: The Red Tower's Mouth
storylines.posterText: Vesryn of Varakush wants you to gather every Fragment of the Red Tower you can find and bring them to the Order. Multi-step contract. 1500 TC and faction standing on completion.

stages.narration: Vesryn spreads a map of the south plains. "We need every Fragment of the Red Tower we can put hands on. There are at least seven scattered across the silt belt. Find them. Bring them. We pay for each."
stages.arbiter: "The Order doesn't ask for this lightly," the Arbiter says. "They're rebuilding something."

stages.narration: You head south. The first Fragment shows up where Vesryn promised — a hexagonal piece of cooled Tartarian iron, still warm. You pocket it.
A second Fragment turns up in an old Reclaimer caravan-wreck. You haggle with the survivor over the price of letting you take it.
A Mud Monarch courier is also looking for the Fragments — they pass you on the road and you stay clear of their notice.
stages.arbiter: "Whoever assembles all seven first wins something we do not yet understand," the Arbiter says.

stages.narration: Third Fragment is in a Sentinel patrol zone. You time the loop.
Fourth and fifth come from a single buried vault. The locking glyphs nearly take your hand off.
Sixth is under an Aether Golem. You don't fight it — you wait until it wanders off and dig where it had been standing.
Seventh is buried in a Mud Spirit's nesting ground. You convince the lesser spirits to let you through.
You assemble all seven and study them. They fit together — partially. Vesryn was right: something is being rebuilt. You carry the bundle back to Varakush.
stages.arbiter: "The Order will not tell you what comes next," the Arbiter says. "But you have done what they could not."

storylines.title: The Path of the True Tartarian
storylines.posterText: Korash of the Deep offers a full True Tartarian ascension trial. Seven steps. Pass them all and the enclave will treat you as one of their own. 1200 TC and major rep.

stages.narration: Korash motions you to sit. "You have shown enough. The trial is seven steps. Refuse any, walk away. Complete them all and the enclave will know you as kin."
stages.arbiter: "This is not a gift the True Tartarians give twice," the Arbiter says.

stages.narration: Step one — the silent pilgrimage. You walk a buried road without speaking, without resting, for the better part of a day.
Step two — the rune trial. A Tartarian glyph is set into a wall. You must read it and trace your name beneath in Aetheric chalk.
Step three — the dive. A flooded antechamber. You swim into the dark with a single torch and bring back what the elders left there.
stages.arbiter: "Most fail here," the Arbiter says. "Do not breathe in."

stages.narration: Step four — the standing watch. You hold the night-shift at the enclave's mouth, alone. Whatever comes by, you do not call for help.
Step five — the fast. You go a full day without rations. The hunger sharpens you. Korash brings you water once.
Step six — the duel. A young Tartarian challenges you to a non-lethal sparring match. You win or lose with honour.
Step seven — the oath. Korash and three elders stand witness. You say the words. They repeat them back. It is done.
stages.arbiter: "You belong to them now, in part," the Arbiter says. "It will count when it counts."

storylines.title: The Reclaimer Relic Run
storylines.posterText: Reclaimers Guild Speaker offers a five-stop relic run — five hidden caches, five takes, no questions. 1000 TC, Guild standing, and a permanent slot on the haul board.

stages.narration: The Speaker hands you a sealed map with five marks. "Each is a relic cache. Hit them in order. You keep nothing of the haul beyond a finder's cut — but you walk out a name in the Guild."
First mark — a half-buried Tartarian utility room. You crack the lock-glyph and pull the haul.
Second mark — a Reclaimer rival has been here recently. You read their tracks, decide they will not be back for hours, and finish the work.
stages.arbiter: "The Guild rewards the quiet ones," the Arbiter says.

stages.narration: Third mark — a Sentinel guards the approach. You time the patrol again and slip past.
Fourth mark — a Mud Spirit nests on top of the cache. You talk it down to a small offering of rations and it lets you in.
Fifth mark — the Speaker did not mention this one is mid-collapse. You dig fast.
You return all five hauls to the Speaker. They count them once, look at you once, and nod.
stages.arbiter: "You are on the board now," the Arbiter says. "That carries weight here."

storylines.title: Silence Across the Border
storylines.posterText: Dr. Lucius Kincaid will pay for a six-stop silencing run — six people who have been talking too loudly about Tartaria. Discretion required. 1300 TC. Monarch standing.

stages.narration: Kincaid passes you a list of six names across a polished table. "All of these have been writing about Tartaria where they should not. We do not require them dead. We require them quiet. Means are your business."
stages.arbiter: "The Monarchs deal in silence," the Arbiter says quietly. "Not in mercy."

stages.narration: First name — a Reclaimer who has been talking to Order scholars. You make a compelling case for them to keep their finds to themselves.
Second name — an Unknowing Masses journalist with a draft article. You take the draft.
Third name — a Forgotten Order scholar's apprentice. You don't approach them directly; you make sure their next field expedition turns up nothing.
Fourth name — a True Tartarian sympathiser in the surface enclave. You convince them you are also a sympathiser.
stages.arbiter: "Lies cost something in this country," the Arbiter says. "Make sure you can pay it."

stages.narration: Fifth name — a Reclaimer's Guild middleman selling photographs of buried sites. You intercept their next courier.
Sixth and last — Kincaid's own former assistant, gone rogue. They expect you. They are not happy.
You return to Kincaid. He counts the items you brought back, looks at you once, and slides a heavy purse across the table.
stages.arbiter: "The Monarchs remember you now," the Arbiter says. "This is not always a gift."

storylines.title: The Ledger of Silence
storylines.posterText: A Mud Monarch factor at the Waystation needs a witness unmade before the Forgotten Order can copy what it saw. Discreet work. 1400 TC and standing.

stages.narration: The factor does not look up from his ledger. "A Guardian stirred at Ostragar. A surveyor of the Order saw it wake and lived. His notes cannot reach Varakush. Nor can he." He slides you a name and a route.
stages.arbiter: "They are not asking you to kill a man," the Arbiter says. "They are asking you to decide the man is a thing. Notice the difference before you agree."

stages.narration: You trace the surveyor to a relay-hut on the Ostragar road. His field-book is gone — copied already, into three fair hands riding for the Order. The factor lied about the count, or did not know it.
You run down the first courier before the Obsidian Pillars and lift the copy from his saddle. He never sees you. One page is torn out — he kept a leaf back, insurance against his own masters.

The second courier is Guild, not Order — a Reclaimer who bought the pages to resell. Coin turns her; she hands them over and tells you the third rider is the surveyor himself, carrying the last leaf to Varakush in person.
stages.arbiter: "Everyone in this errand is selling something," the Arbiter murmurs. "Ask yourself what you are selling, and to whom."

stages.narration: You catch the surveyor on the Varakush approach. He does not run. "I saw it open its eyes," he says. "You can take my book. You cannot take that I saw it." He offers you the last leaf — and a choice the factor never mentioned.

You return to the Waystation with every copy. The factor burns them one page at a time and pays you in silence. "The world sleeps a little longer," he says. Whether that is mercy or a leash, he does not say, and you do not ask.
stages.arbiter: "You bought the world quiet," the Arbiter says. "Quiet is not the same as safe. Remember who profits from the difference."

storylines.title: The Descent to Karok-Sa
storylines.posterText: The True Tartarians will pay a surface-walker to escort a reconsecration party down into buried Karok-Sa and see it done. 1600 TC and deep standing.

stages.narration: The enclave-mother marks a shaft on your palm in ash. "Karok-Sa held a Giant-shrine before the Flood took it. The Aether there has gone sour and the way is fouled. Walk our pilgrims down, keep them breathing, and light the shrine again."
stages.arbiter: "They are trusting you with their faithful, not their coin," the Arbiter says. "That is the harder thing to be given. Do not spend it cheaply."

stages.narration: The upper stair of Karok-Sa is choked with silt-glass and old flood-wrack. You read the safe line the way the pilgrims read prayer — one wrong slab is a drop into black water. You find the seam that holds.

Halfway down the air turns to poison — Aether gone rancid, a haze that stops breath. The pilgrims falter. You draw the bad Aether off with a working, buying the party a corridor of clean air one lungful wide.
Something in the drowned nave has been alone a very long time. A Shifting Shade, born of the soured field, walks out of a wall between you and the shrine and will not let the faithful pass.
stages.arbiter: "It was a person once, or it was never anything," the Arbiter says. "Down here the two look the same. Put it down and move on."

stages.narration: At the shrine the eldest pilgrim breaks — this was her birth-city, drowned when she was a child. She will not leave. You talk her back from the edge of the black water, and she gives you the relighting-word her mother taught her.

You speak the word and the shrine takes light — and beneath it, a Mud Golem the size of the nave opens one eye, a Giant-Watch construct that has waited in the dark for someone to wake it. The pilgrims kneel. You do not have that luxury.
stages.arbiter: "They call it a guardian," the Arbiter says quietly. "It has forgotten what it guards. That makes it no gentler. Finish this."

stages.narration: The construct stills, judged you not an enemy, and folds back into the dark. The shrine burns steady behind you as the pilgrims climb home singing. The enclave-mother washes the ash from your palm herself. "You are one of the deep now," she says.

storylines.title: Blood of the Aetherborn
storylines.posterText: A Dynasty proctor at the Border Post seeks proof of a claimant's Aetherborn bloodline — a relic only the pure may touch and live. 1800 TC and standing for a clean result.

stages.narration: The proctor speaks of bloodlines the way a butcher speaks of cuts. "A claimant petitions the Dynasty. Before he is raised or discarded, his blood must be tested against the Vein-Reliquary in the Sinking Cathedral. Fetch it. The relic decides; we merely watch."
stages.arbiter: "Only the pure deserve to inherit," the Arbiter recites flatly. "Every empire that has said those words has meant: only the useful. Watch which one they mean here."

stages.narration: The Sinking Cathedral takes on a hand-span of water an hour. You find the reliquary vault by following the Aether — the relic sings to the flooded stone. The last party to seek it is here too, drowned at the vault door, Dynasty seals on their coats.
The vault seal breaks and the Cathedral answers by dropping a floor. You take the Vein-Reliquary and run the falling stair ahead of the flood, water at your heels the whole black length of it.

Above ground the claimant finds you first — a frightened young man who has read what the relic does to the impure. "It burns the false to ash," he says. "I do not know what I am. Test me here, away from them, and tell me the truth before they make it a spectacle."
stages.arbiter: "He is asking you for mercy the Dynasty does not stock," the Arbiter says. "Whatever the relic says, remember you were the one he asked."

stages.narration: At the Border Post the proctor lays the claimant's hand to the Vein-Reliquary before the assembled court — and the relic wakes wrong, an Aetheric Apparition tearing loose from the old blood inside it, judging every soul in the room impure at once.
stages.arbiter: "The relic does not care about bloodlines," the Arbiter says. "It cares about hunger. They woke it hungry. Now everyone here is on the menu, purity be damned."

stages.narration: You put the Apparition down before it can render its verdict on the court. The proctor pays you and records the claimant as "inconclusive" — a word that will follow the young man to his grave, but leaves him with one. It is the most mercy the Dynasty knows how to file.

storylines.title: The Giant-Watch Vigil
storylines.posterText: The Servants of the Giants have felt the ground breathe at the Giant Vault. They will pay a steady hand to stand the vigil and read what stirs. 1500 TC and standing.

stages.narration: The vigil-keeper at the Giant-Watch Shrine presses your ear to the stone. Far below, a slow tremor, like breath. "A Giant turns in its sleep beneath the Vault," she says. "The order splits over it — wake it, or let it dream. Stand the vigil with me and help us read the truth of it."
stages.arbiter: "Faith and geology feel the same tremor differently," the Arbiter observes. "One of them is easier to be wrong about. Keep both eyes open."

stages.narration: You descend to the Vault door and read the tremor at its source. It is no Giant — it is the Aetheric field feeding a dormant Guardian below, cycling toward a wake it was never meant to reach. The faithful have mistaken a machine's hunger for a god's breath.

You climb back to a schism. The zealots want to fling the Vault open and greet their god; the elders want it sealed forever. You tell them what you found. Half call you a liar sent by the Order. You talk the vigil-keeper into hearing the rest.
stages.arbiter: "You have just told the devout their god is a boiler," the Arbiter says. "Do not expect thanks. Expect a knife, and hope for a hearing."

stages.narration: The zealots move to break the seal that night regardless. You slip into the Vault ahead of them to reach the Guardian's core-cycle before their torches do — one closing valve between the faithful and a waking machine.

You reach the core-cycle as the seal gives. The dormant Guardian — a Steam Walker grown vast on a century of stray Aether — hauls upright in the dark, and the zealots pour in singing to meet it, mistaking its rise for rapture.
stages.arbiter: "They will call it a miracle right up until it kills them," the Arbiter says. "Give them a chance to be wrong and alive. Bring it down."

stages.narration: You still the Guardian and the singing stops. The vigil-keeper seals the Vault with her own hands and names you Watch-Kin. "It was not our god," she tells the shaken faithful. "But something down there kept our god's house. That is worth a vigil still."

storylines.title: Scripture in Stone
storylines.posterText: A Stone Builder lodge-master at the Survey Camp needs the Architectural Sorcery of the Grand Spire read before his lodge cracks apart under it. 1500 TC and standing.

stages.narration: The lodge-master unrolls a rubbing of a wall from the Grand Spire of Etheria. "The Tartarians wrote their engineering into their stone — load, Aether, and prayer in one script. We copied a passage into our lodge and now the lodge groans at night. Read the original before it comes down on us."
stages.arbiter: "They built a thing they did not understand and are surprised it does not love them," the Arbiter says. "An old story. Read carefully; the stone will not repeat itself."

stages.narration: At the Grand Spire you find the source passage — and the Builders' copy was wrong by one glyph, a load-line read as a prayer-line. The Spire's own version routes the Aether down and out. The lodge's routes it in, and up, into a room full of people.

The Spire will not simply give up its reading. The passage is live — Architectural Sorcery still flowing through it after a thousand years. You match the working, hold the flow steady, and copy the true glyph while the wall hums under your hand.

The correction destabilizes the ancient course. A pillar leaning "precariously" since before the Flood finally chooses to fall. You take the true reading and clear the collapsing gallery a half-step ahead of the stone.
stages.arbiter: "Knowledge, then the ceiling," the Arbiter says. "Tartaria charges for both in the same coin. Run."

stages.narration: You reach the lodge as the miswritten wall reaches its limit — the trapped Aether tearing loose as an Aetheric Salamander, all the stored heat of a bad translation given teeth, loose among the apprentices.
stages.arbiter: "Their scripture caught fire," the Arbiter says. "Put it out before it takes the congregation. Then teach them to read."

stages.narration: You correct the lodge-wall with the true glyph and the groaning stops. The lodge-master carves your name small among the founders. "Tartaria's buildings were scripture," he says, humbled. "We were reciting it wrong. You taught us to read a single verse. It was almost the end of us."

storylines.title: Sasha's Gambit
storylines.posterText: Sasha Ironheart of the Revivalists wants a core-line at the Aetheric Chamber brought back to life — and she needs a blade willing to risk a Second Flood to do it. 2000 TC and standing.

stages.narration: Sasha Ironheart does not soften it. "Every other faction tinkers at the edges. I mean to switch Tartaria back on. One core-line at the Aetheric Chamber, reactivated. Yes, it could flood the world again. Doing nothing floods it slower. Are you a blade or a bystander?"
stages.arbiter: "She is the only one honest enough to name the risk," the Arbiter says. "That does not make her right. It makes her dangerous with the lights on. Decide how far you will follow."

stages.narration: You survey the Aetheric Chamber's dead core-line. Three of Sasha's cells got here first and left notes in the dust — one warns the line will overload, one says it will hold, one is simply a name and a date. The cells share a goal and not a method, and it shows.

A Forgotten Order team has come to sabotage the reactivation before it starts — moderates who think Sasha will drown them all. You slip past them to the core housing without a shot fired. Whether that was loyalty or doubt, you keep to yourself.
stages.arbiter: "You just chose Sasha over the people trying to stop a flood," the Arbiter says. "Sit with that. The story is not done choosing you back."

stages.narration: The core-line wakes under your working, Aether roaring back into a channel dry for a century. It surges past every safe mark — Sasha's optimistic cell was wrong. You wrestle the flow toward the overload cell's cutoff, the one everyone else ignored.

The overloading line births a Guardian meant to bleed off exactly this — an Aetheric Apparition of pure surplus power, loosed to protect Tartaria from its own revival by killing whoever caused it. It comes for you and Sasha both.
stages.arbiter: "The empire built a failsafe against people like her," the Arbiter says. "It is doing its job. Survive it, and decide afterward whether it was right."

stages.narration: You bring the Apparition down and hold the line at a hair below flood. One core-line lives — a single lit window in a drowned house. Sasha looks at it and, for once, is quiet. "Not the world," she says. "Yet. But now they know it can be done. So do you."
stages.arbiter: "You left a light on in a house that drowned a civilization," the Arbiter says. "History will decide if that was hope or the first drop. So, eventually, will you."

storylines.title: The Highest Bidder
storylines.posterText: A Reclaimer broker at the Hidden Market needs a neutral blade to run a relic auction that three factions all mean to win by force. 1700 TC and standing.

stages.narration: The broker taps a strongbox. "One relic. A Guardian control-key — points a dormant construct at whatever you like. The Order, the Dynasty, and the Monarchs all bid. I need someone who owes none of them to run the floor and keep me breathing when the loser draws steel."
stages.arbiter: "You are not selling a relic," the Arbiter says. "You are selling the right to aim a god. Whoever wins, someone dies later. Keep that in your ledger."

stages.narration: You case the Market floor before the bell. All three bidders came heavy — Order sappers by the east stalls, a Dynasty duelist working the shadows, a Monarch factor with coin enough to buy the building. None of them plans to lose an auction.

You open the floor and hold it with your voice alone, letting the bids climb while the room decides whether to be civilized. The Dynasty duelist tests you once, quietly. You cool it without a blade. The price triples.
stages.arbiter: "You are conducting a room full of loaded guns," the Arbiter says. "The music is the only thing keeping them holstered. Do not stop playing."

stages.narration: The Monarch factor moves to end the auction his way — a signal to torch the strongbox rather than let a rival have the key. You slip the box out from under his fire and into the broker's hands before the flames find it.

With coin no longer able to settle it, the losers settle it the old way — the Order sappers and the Dynasty duelist turning on each other and on you across the burning floor. The broker cowers behind the box.
stages.arbiter: "The auction is over," the Arbiter says. "The war it started is not. Cut your way to the door."

stages.narration: You break clear with the broker and the box both intact. He pays you in the quiet after, hands shaking. "The winner gets the key tomorrow," he says. "You could take it tonight." The strongbox sits between you, and for one breath the aim of a Guardian is yours to set.
stages.arbiter: "Every faction wanted this and you are the one holding it," the Arbiter says. "That is not luck. That is a test. Answer it as yourself."

storylines.title: The Silence Protocol
storylines.posterText: A Conspiracy Architect handler needs a leak at Voronov closed before the Unknowing Masses learn what sleeps under their city. Total discretion. 1600 TC and standing.

stages.narration: The handler speaks in the flat voice of someone who has done this before. "A Voronov schoolmaster found a Tartarian relay under his town and started teaching from it. Children are drawing Aether-glyphs in their primers. The Protocol is simple: the lesson stops. How, we leave to you."
stages.arbiter: "The lie is a kindness. The silence is a service," the Arbiter says. "They will keep telling you that until you believe it. Notice the moment you do."

stages.narration: In Voronov you find the relay exactly as reported — and the schoolmaster is no zealot, just a curious man who found a wonder and could not keep it to himself. The glyphs in the children's primers are, God help you, correct.

You could burn the relay and the man with it — the Protocol's usual reading. Instead you sit with the schoolmaster and learn what he actually knows. Less than the handler fears. Enough to matter. He is not afraid of you. That is the hardest part.
stages.arbiter: "He thinks you came to learn," the Arbiter says. "You came to close a mouth. The distance between those is the whole of your character. Mind it."

stages.narration: A Monarch cutter has also come for the leak — the Architects' patrons prefer their silences permanent. You reach the relay ahead of the knife and pull its core, leaving the schoolmaster a dead machine and a live pulse.

The pulled core does not want to die quiet — it discharges its stored century of Aether as a Shifting Shade in the empty schoolhouse, and the children are still filing out. You put yourself between them and it.
stages.arbiter: "The relay would rather scream than be silenced too," the Arbiter says. "So would the man. So, one day, might you. End this without ending them."

stages.narration: You bring the handler a dead relay and a report that reads "contained." What you left in Voronov — a frightened schoolmaster, a town of children who saw a wonder and were told to forget it — is the part of the Protocol that has no line on the form. You wrote that line yourself.
stages.arbiter: "You served the silence," the Arbiter says. "Or you served the man. The Architects will only read one of those in your report. You will carry the other."

storylines.title: The Drowned Library
storylines.posterText: Vesryn of the Forgotten Order seeks a scholar to recover the Aetheric treatises lost in the flooding of the Sunken Enclave — the Order's deepest archive. 1800 TC and standing.

stages.narration: Vesryn lays a hand on an empty shelf. "The Sunken Enclave held every treatise we ever recovered. When it flooded we saved the readers, not the reading. Aether-proof cases keep the pages down there yet. Bring back what you can. Choose well — you cannot carry it all."
stages.arbiter: "Knowledge that drowned once will drown you gladly," the Arbiter says. "Take what you can bear, and forgive yourself the rest."

stages.narration: You dive the Enclave and find the stacks by lamplight, cases glinting in the silt. The catalogue is intact — you can read what each case holds before you spend your air lifting it. Some are cures. Some are weapons. Some are only beautiful.

The deepest stack is warded — Tartarian ink that eats light and lungs both. You hold a working over your own breath and read past the ward to a case marked in the Enclave's founder's own hand: the treatise on the cores themselves.

Lifting the founder's case wakes the Enclave's failsafe — the flood meant to keep exactly this from leaving. The water rises to reclaim its library. You run the drowning stacks with your chosen cases, air and archive both running out.
stages.arbiter: "The Order built a tomb to protect its own knowledge from itself," the Arbiter says. "It is working. Get out before it works on you."

stages.narration: At the Enclave mouth an Aetheric Ooze — grown fat on a century of dissolved ink and lost thought — bars the only stair. It has read, in its way, everything that dissolved into it. You cut through the sum of the Order's losses to reach the light.
stages.arbiter: "Everything the Order forgot ended up in that thing," the Arbiter says. "It is very well read. Kill it anyway."

stages.narration: You lay your salvage on Vesryn's table — a handful of what once filled a hall. He reads the founder's treatise on the cores and goes very still. "This changes what we thought we knew about the Flood," he says. "You chose these pages. You should be here when we learn what they mean."

storylines.title: The Purge at Asgardar
storylines.posterText: A Dynasty enforcer at Asgardar needs a discreet hand to help "reconcile" a bloodline that has grown impure — quietly, before the court notices. 1900 TC and standing.

stages.narration: The enforcer will not say the word "kill." "A cadet branch at Asgardar has thinned. Their blood no longer reads pure. The court would spend them in the machines. I would rather retire them quietly, with their dignity. Help me do the merciful thing." He believes it.
stages.arbiter: "He calls a purge a mercy and means it," the Arbiter says. "That is worse than a man who lies. Watch where his mercy runs out."

stages.narration: At Asgardar you find the cadet branch — an old woman and her grandchildren, tending a border-shrine, harming no one. Their blood is "impure" by a fraction the machines would never notice. Someone at court wants their estate, and purity is the lever.

The matriarch knows exactly why you have come. "The Dynasty eats its own to prove it is still hungry," she says, unafraid. "You could carry back that we are already dead. Or you could carry the truth, and be spent for it." She hands you the estate's true bloodline record.
stages.arbiter: "She is asking you to risk the machines in her place," the Arbiter says. "That is a great deal to ask a stranger. It is also fair. Decide which you weigh heavier."

stages.narration: The court's real agent — the one who wants the estate — moves to make the purge permanent before you can report otherwise. You reach the shrine ahead of his blades and put the cadet family behind you.

Cornered, the court's agent throws the shrine's own defense at you — a Vein-Reliquary Apparition roused to "test" the impure, aimed at the family it was built to protect. You stand between the Dynasty's cruelty and its excuse.
stages.arbiter: "They built the relic to purge the impure," the Arbiter says. "Now it cannot tell the family from the assassin. Neither, it seems, could the Dynasty. End it."

stages.narration: You bring the enforcer the estate's true record and the court agent's severed scheme. He reads it, and for the first time his certainty cracks. "Retired quietly," he writes, and lets the cadet branch live. Whether you saved a family or just delayed a machine, you made the Dynasty blink. It is not nothing.
stages.arbiter: "You did not fix the Dynasty," the Arbiter says. "You made one of its knives hesitate. In an empire of the certain, a hesitation is a revolution. Small. Real."
